title: The Pneumatics of Hero of Alexandria from the original Greek
locator: 1851 edition: editor's preface pp. vii–viii; §50, p. 72 (Pneumatica II.11 in another numbering).
scope_limit: Digitised English edition, not an ancient manuscript or apparatus. Ancient author's exact date and the corpus's transmission are uncertain. Editorial heading is not Hero's terminology. No productive-load test or adoption count in the cited passage.
evidence_lineage: A nineteenth-century translation and editorial reconstruction of a transmitted Greek textual tradition. It is the textual object examined by later scholarship, not independent confirmation of physical deployment.

title: The Mechanical Tradition of Hero of Alexandria: Strategies of Reading from Antiquity to the Early Modern Period
locator: Publisher's 10-page Introduction excerpt, especially pp. 1–4; publisher metadata distinguishes first publication 2023 from paperback 2025.
scope_limit: Only introductory excerpt inspected, not full book. Keyser's original 1992 analysis was encountered through Roby and was not acquired. Purpose of the sphere remains an interpretation.
evidence_lineage: Close interpretation of the Heronian corpus and its reception; shares the ancient textual tradition with ANC-S01. The discussion of Keyser is inherited scholarship, not a separately inspected source.

title: The second century CE Roman watermills of Barbegal: Unraveling the enigma of one of the oldest industrial complexes
locator: Science Advances 4(9), eaar3620. Introduction; Results: microstratigraphy, crystal structure, stable isotope composition; Fig. 4; Discussion. Full article XML acquired at https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC6124920/fullTextXML after publisher/PMC browser access failed.
scope_limit: Carbonate samples record selected structures and years. Seasonal interruptions are better supported than identification of customers or hardtack production. Wider claims about Roman growth and empire-wide crises are not independently established here.
evidence_lineage: Original analysis of carbonate fragments from the 1930s Barbegal excavations, surviving museum material and site evidence. ANC-S04 reanalyses overlapping material; the two papers are not independent replications.

title: Operation and decline of the Barbegal mill complex, the largest industrial complex of antiquity
locator: Geoarchaeology 39, pp. 594–608; §§2–5 and especially §6, pp. 606–607. PDF acquired from https://openscience.ub.uni-mainz.de/server/api/core/bitstreams/ed058e41-ee6f-4841-b767-2e2c2dfddaaf/content .
scope_limit: Three reconstructed flumes from the western train do not represent every mill or establish owner identity, profits, or a unique abandonment cause. Do not adopt the title's world-scale superlative as a measured comparative finding.
evidence_lineage: Further analysis and reconstruction of the Barbegal carbonate archive also used by ANC-S03. Adds microstratigraphic/hydraulic interpretation; shares authors, specimens, and much archaeological chronology.

title: The Aqueducts of Rome (De aquaeductu urbis Romae), Book II
locator: Ancient account c. 97–early second century CE; Loeb English edition. Inspected §§94–96, 116–129, especially §§116–118 (workforce and funding), 121–124 (repair scheduling and access).
scope_limit: Official self-presentation and prescriptions are not audited performance records. Reported staffing and finances are for Rome at a particular time, not the entire empire. Translation uses 'wages' for expenses of enslaved gangs; this does not establish free contractual employment.
evidence_lineage: Transmitted text by an imperial water commissioner, including quoted earlier legal measures. Bannon (ANC-S06) uses this same source alongside inscriptions and juristic texts; overlapping propositions are not independent corroboration.

title: Fresh Water in Roman Law: Rights and Policy
locator: Journal of Roman Studies 107, pp. 60–89; inspected Introduction, §III Civic Aqueducts, especially private grants and provincial examples, and §V Conclusion; full Cambridge HTML.
scope_limit: Reconstruction from selected legal, epigraphic and literary evidence, principally late Republic through early Empire. Rights on paper do not measure household access or equal enforcement. Ancient-law analysis, not current legal guidance.
evidence_lineage: Original legal-historical synthesis of Frontinus, municipal inscriptions, and juristic texts transmitted in Justinian's Digest. Specific inscriptions were read through Bannon, not separately inspected; part of the evidence overlaps ANC-S05.

title: Wars, Book V (Gothic War I), chapter 19
locator: Gothic War I.19.8–28 (= Wars V.19.8–28), especially §§13 and 19–28; Loeb volume III.
scope_limit: Literary account of the siege of Rome in 537, written later in the sixth century. Credits Belisarius; statements that mills sufficed for the city are not output measurements. Does not establish the permanent fate of every aqueduct.
evidence_lineage: Ancient narrative with close authorial proximity to the campaign, surviving through textual transmission. The emergency sequence is a single narrative witness, not an independently replicated operational log.

title: Qanāt and Falaj: Polycentric and Multi-Period Innovations: Iran and the United Arab Emirates as Case Studies
locator: Underground Aqueducts Handbook, chapter 17, pp. 279–301; inspected chapter OCR, especially §§17.1–17.2.3 (pp. 280–288) and §§17.3.4–17.4.2 (pp. 293–295).
scope_limit: Archaeological synthesis with explicit disagreements, including shallow versus deeper sources and early Iranian dating. Most underlying excavation reports and luminescence datasets were not acquired. Polycentric origins are argued, not established at every site.
evidence_lineage: Author's comparative archaeological interpretation, drawing on excavations at al-Madam and other UAE sites plus previous Iranian studies. Its treatment of Polybius overlaps ANC-S09; chronology is not an independent dataset for every repeated later citation.

title: Histories, Book X, chapter 28
locator: X.28.1–7, especially §§2–4; Loeb volume IV, pp. 169–171. Describes Antiochus III's Parthian campaign, conventionally 209 BCE, from a later second-century BCE account.
scope_limit: Reports local testimony about earlier Persian rule; not an original grant or construction account. Paton's wording is five generations of cultivation rights, not an explicit tax exemption. The water source is not technically specified. Host notes this page is not fully proofread.
evidence_lineage: Single ancient transmitted narrative. Boucharlat (ANC-S08) critically interprets the same passage. Reading both does not give two independent witnesses to the grant policy.

title: Dujiangyan's Annual Repair System in Ancient Times: From Jianpengyan Inscription by Shu Defender Li Bing in Qin Dynasty (古代都江堰岁修制度——从《秦蜀守李冰湔堋堰官碑》说起)
locator: Journal of Xihua University (Philosophy & Social Sciences) 37(4), pp. 8–18, DOI 10.19642/j.issn.1672-8505.2018.04.002. Inspected attributed Chinese reproduction §§1–5, especially §§1, 2, 4. Publisher metadata/abstract verified; journal PDF failed (404/412).
scope_limit: Substantial reproduction, not independently collated against journal PDF; some apparatus may be missing. English summaries here are our translations. Inscription dates/readings are mediated by Peng; no original rubbing inspected. Qin continuity arguments and triumphal framing require scrutiny.
evidence_lineage: Original historian's argument using excavated Han inscriptions, transmitted histories, and much later records. These are several underlying sources but only Peng's presentation was inspected; modern claims of continuous operation are not independent evidence for each intervening century.

title: Sustainability of the Dujiangyan Irrigation System for over 2000 Years—A Numerical Investigation of the Water and Sediment Dynamic Diversions
locator: Sustainability 12, 2431; §§1, 3–6, especially pp. 2–3 and 12–13. PDF acquired from https://mdpi-res.com/d_attachment/sustainability/sustainability-12-02431/article_deploy/sustainability-12-02431.pdf .
scope_limit: Numerical experiment using particular channel geometry and flow regimes, not an ancient measurement. Omits modern upstream dam effect; notes 1974 modification and further validation needs. Introductory claims of perfectly continuous performance and abandoned ancient systems elsewhere are not accepted as historical findings.
evidence_lineage: Original coupled flow/sediment model drawing on earlier hydraulic studies; historical origin and continuity statements are inherited background. Independent of Peng's inscription analysis for physical modelling, but not an independent historical time series.

title: Archaeological studies at Dholavira using GPR
locator: Current Science 114(4), pp. 879–887; methods pp. 880–881; interpretations pp. 884–886; Conclusion p. 886. Institutional PDF inspected at https://asc.iitgn.ac.in/assets/publications/research_papers/Archaeological_studies_at_Dholavira_using_GPR_Agrawal_Majumder_Bisht_Prashant.pdf .
scope_limit: Unexcavated features and proposed flood mechanism are hypotheses requiring excavation. Abstract/early text gives 12,276 m² but conclusion gives 12,776 m²; exact survey area not adopted. GPR dates the survey, not the ancient destruction.
evidence_lineage: Original GPR measurements collected in 2015, interpreted using existing excavation knowledge, including coauthor Bisht's work. Measurement is new; contextual interpretations partly share the ASI excavation lineage summarised by ANC-S13.

title: Dholavira: A Harappan City (India), No 1645—Advisory Body Evaluation
locator: 13-page standalone evaluation; printed pp. 13–15, especially Description and history, phased settlement and water structures; full PDF accessible through web extraction.
scope_limit: Evaluation based on State Party nomination, excavation material and mission evidence, not the full excavation report. Historical dates and destruction narrative were not independently re-dated. Overall c. 3000–1500 BCE label includes gaps and a final phase reported as c. 1500–1450 BCE.
evidence_lineage: Institutional synthesis relying heavily on ASI excavation and nomination evidence. Shares parts of the archaeological lineage with ANC-S12; does not independently corroborate each reconstruction or proposed cause of decline.
